Silverstone 2023 · Qualifying · Norris / Piastri

A closer look at Norris's 0.131s advantage

On lap 25, Norris gained 0.090s in sector 1. His sampled minimum speed in the first slow-speed zone was 98km/h, compared with Piastri's 93km/h. Their full-throttle transition intervals overlapped.

The next comparison should focus on deceleration and minimum speed. The available samples do not establish an earlier return to full throttle.

Evidence and interpretation

Both laps use source-reported fresh soft tyres with a tyre age of 1 at lap start and a green track status. Their starts were 4.324s apart; fuel, setup and tow conditions are not controlled.

Lap 25 · Norris minus Piastri; negative means Norris is quicker
Reported timingNorrisPiastriDifference
Lap86.961s87.092s−0.131s
Sector 127.544s27.634s−0.090s
Sector 235.312s35.350s−0.038s
Sector 324.105s24.108s−0.003s

Candidate mechanism. Zone 1 spans 13.6–27.2% of estimated reference progress. Norris's higher sampled minimum suggests a difference around the slowest part of the zone. The first ≥95% throttle transition after that minimum falls at 18.71–19.00% for Norris and 18.68–18.94% for Piastri. Those brackets overlap; they do not establish earlier recovery or equal exit performance.

What the data cannot settle. The zone's time difference is unavailable because position coverage does not support its boundaries. At the sector 1 boundary, position-derived and reported time differences disagree by about 0.045s. This is a consistency check, not an error bound: the full 0.090s sector advantage cannot be assigned to this zone or phase.

Next engineering step. Compare deceleration and minimum-speed behaviour on laps with matched conditions before considering a setup change. On lap 22, Norris was 0.658s slower overall; tyre ages and start times differ. Lap 25 alone does not establish a repeatable driver trait or identify a tyre-grip or vehicle-balance cause.

    Load session context to inspect SC/VSC messages alongside the assumptions.

    One same-compound tyre change within the chosen horizon: delayed stop total minus pit-now total. Positive = pit now is quicker in this model. Equal pit loss, fuel terms and equal warm-up penalties cancel between these candidates. Green pit loss only changes the SC/VSC saving. No race-position, mandatory-compound, traffic, gap or out-lap prediction; no optimal-strategy claim. Qualifying laps do not identify race tyre degradation.

    Methodology

    Selected-lap alignment

    Prediction checks

    All-session coverage, errors and reproduction: practice, qualifying, race and sprint are audited separately. A recent-pace forecast requires three usable same-stint laps; shorter runs show references only. The earlier four-race check below uses a different, traffic-filtered population.

    Historical forecasts use only laps completed by the cutoff. The existing regression is compared with a recent-three-lap mean on the same supported targets. Missing traffic coverage, neutralisation, pit laps and model holds are reported separately. Replacement checks freeze the latest prior fit of the same compound before the actual stop; they do not validate alternative stop schedules, pit-loss assumptions or tyre temperature.
